comments.content: TS2365/TS7052/TS2532/TS2339/TS2575 — `pv.ops` is typed `Record<string, unknown>[]` (via `Array.isArray(pv.ops)` check), so iterating `for (const op of ops)` infers `op` as `unknown`, causing compile errors on every access: `op.action`, `op.target`, `op.dest`, and the `unknown op action ${op.action}` log. Fix: type `ops` as `PreviewOp[]` (import from ./types.ts) — e.g. `const ops = (Array.isArray(pv.ops) ? pv.ops : []) as PreviewOp[];` — or cast elements in the loop (`for (const op of ops as PreviewOp[])`).

TS2339 — `pv.ops`, `pv.previewId`, `pv.keep`, `pv.measuredAt` are accessed on `PreviewDoc` (=`PlanCleanJson & Record<string, unknown>`). If `PlanCleanJson` is not imported/used as a constraint, these may fail to resolve. Verify `import type { PlanCleanJson }` is present and these fields are declared. (Already imported — OK.)

Missing `await run(process.argv.slice(2))` error handling — at the bottom, `if (import.meta.main) { await run(...); }` is top-level-await in an ESM/bun module. Uncaught promise rejections from `run()` (e.g., `loadPreview` network/IO errors) surface as unhandled rejections. Consider wrapping in try/catch and exiting non-zero. (Minor, but consistency matters for a CLI entry.)

In `run()`, the branch detection: `a.includes("execute")` will trigger `runExecute` even if a user passes `--id execute` (treating the literal id 'execute' as an action). Low risk but semantically fragile — consider checking `--approved` presence before the bare `execute` string. Also `a.includes("execute")` is O(n) on a possibly small array — acceptable, not flagged.
comments.existing_code:
if (a.includes("execute") || a.includes("--approved") || parseApproved(a) !== null) {
    await runExecute(a);

comments.content: `loadFromFiles` scans `STORE_DIR` with `new Glob("preview-*.json")` — if `STORE_DIR` does not exist, `glob.scan` throws (not all Bun versions throw synchronously; some emit). The code catches it, which is correct. No defect. (Acknowledged, no comment needed.)

`verifyShas` lowercases `live` via comparison `live !== sha.toLowerCase()`. `measureHead` returns the hash already lowercase (git output is hex), and `sha` regex is case-insensitive. This comparison is robust — OK. No defect.
